content.title: About
content.content: A custard-filled doughnut with icing is a sweet fried pastry shaped like a ring, filled with smooth custard and topped with a glossy icing. The dough is typically made from wheat flour, yeast, milk, eggs and sugar, then deep‑fried until golden.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Doughnuts became popular in the United States in the 19th century after originating in Europe.
The custard filling is often made from egg yolks, sugar and milk, giving it a silky texture.
Icing can be chocolate, vanilla or fruit‑flavored, depending on preference.
Traditional toppings include sprinkles, nuts or fresh berries.
In many countries doughnuts are enjoyed with hot coffee or tea as a morning snack.

items.title: Quick energy source
items.content: The carbohydrate and sugar content provides a rapid boost of energy.

items.title: Calcium from dairy
items.content: Milk and cream used in the dough and custard supply calcium for bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeast and eggs add B1, B2 and B6 vitamins that support metabolism.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive sugar in the icing and custard can raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Saturated and trans fats
items.content: Deep‑frying adds saturated fats and sometimes trans fats, which are best limited.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Doughnuts may contain milk, eggs, wheat and nuts (if used in the icing), which are common allergens.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Doughnuts are usually served at room temperature. They can be eaten as a standalone treat, split open for extra filling, or paired with a hot beverage.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep doughnuts in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a zip‑lock bag and reheat in the oven before serving.
